thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P1 paging alert — serving-runtime: sustained swap/paging + GPU OOMs in us-east-2. Multiple containers flapping. Autoescalation to incidents channel.

incident-bot: Affected service: continuous-batcher (runtime). Symptoms: micro-latency spikes -> long tail -> queue growth -> container OOMs. First sign ~ 2026-03-14T23:54:38Z.

sara-ops: saw it spike around 23:53 — queues went from ~200 -> 10k in 3m. node fs/paging iowait high. GPU OOM logs show KV cache growth + repeated replays.

jenna-oncall: I'm on it. tagging @mike-rt and @alexa-sre. Is there an automatic fallback route?

mike-rt: we have a fallback model pool but routing isn't triggering because batcher hasn't returned errors — it's just very high latency. hard to hit the fallback policy.

kevin-ml: this looks like the recent scheduler tweak (adaptive-slab) allowed batches to accumulate when memory pressure hit -> livelock where queue adders never backpress. Could be the regression from merge r/3456.

alexa-sre: confirmed node flapping: kubelet restarting container runtime on three hosts: us-east-2a-{12,14,19}. system logs show repeated OOM kills.

jenna-oncall: action plan: 1) disable continuous-batcher on serving runtime (flip feature flag) 2) scale dedicated pool + cordon bad nodes 3) enable fallback routing to cpu-only smaller model 4) collect debug tarball and flamegraphs. I'll handoff at 00:15Z.

sara-ops: doing step 1 now — flipping flag in k/v config. command: ```
# disable continuous batching at runtime
curl -XPOST $ADMIN_API/flags/continuous_batcher -d '{"enabled":false}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN'
```

sara-ops: flag accepted. Observing backlog drainers kicking in. queue size shown in metrics: 9.8k -> 4.1k within 45s.

mike-rt: pushing routing override: ```
POST /routing/override
{ "selector": "service==continuous-batcher", "route_to": "model-cpu-small", "ttl": 600 }
``` Should reduce GPU memory pressure.

tara-cust: FYI, customer Alpha reported 503s, support ticket #INC-9843. They want ETA.

jenna-oncall: short answer: mitigation in progress, expect degraded latency for ~10-20m while we drain. I'll update customer comms.

alexa-sre: cordoning nodes now: ```
kubectl cordon us-east-2a-12
kubectl drain us-east-2a-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
``` Draining replicated workloads to other AZs.

kevin-ml: looking at model runtime stats — KV cache per-session memory shoots up with long sequences, and the batching livelock means caches aren't evicted. Patch idea: enforce per-batch KV cap + early-error on enqueue when node memory > 80%.

sara-ops: restarted batcher containers on 2 nodes after drain. container restart seemed to free memory but one node re-flapped after 30s.

mike-rt: snapshot of OOM log: ```
[2026-03-14T23:56:12Z] runtime: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[2026-03-14T23:56:12Z] batcher: queue size 12124, inflight=0, enqueue rate spike
[2026-03-14T23:56:12Z] kernel: oom-killer invoked, container id abc123 terminated
```

jenna-oncall: I'm going to create a short-lived autoscale (add 6 GPU nodes) to buy headroom while we fully revert scheduler change. @sara-ops please coordinate with infra.

sara-ops: request to infra for +6 g4dn equivalent nodes submitted. ETA ~5m.

alexa-sre: adding pressure relief: I'm increasing swapiness threshold and dropping dirty background writing to reduce iowait and paging storm: ```
echo 10 > /proc/sys/vm/swappiness
sysctl -w vm.dirty_ratio=5
```

mike-rt: routing override is live; traffic to cpu-small pool at ~40% of traffic now. Latency p50 still elevated but p95/p99 improving.

kevin-ml: I reverted the adaptive-slab commit in a canary: ```
git revert r/3456 --no-ff
bazel build //runtime/batcher:service && deploy canary --target=batcher-canary
``` Canary looks stable for 2m (no queue runaway).

jenna-oncall: good. I will roll the revert to production after 5m of stability in canary. Handing off to @mike-rt for post-mitigation routing and customer notes. I'll remain reachable.

mike-rt: rolling revert to prod now. Gate: healthchecks green. Rolling restart triggers; monitor closely.

sara-ops: infra reports new nodes up and joined cluster. queue size now 1.2k and trending down. OOMs stopped 00:04Z.

tara-cust: Customer Alpha updated: reduced 503s but still seeing some elevated latency; they asked for postmortem.

mike-rt: short incident summary for now: root cause — regression in continuous-batcher scheduler (r/3456) allowed unbounded batch growth under memory pressure -> queue livelock + KV-cache thrash -> GPU OOMs -> container restarts -> node flaps. Mitigations: feature-flag disable, routing override to cpu pool, cordon/drain flapping nodes, revert scheduler change, temporary scale up. Impact: several customers saw 5-20m of 5xxs and high latency (p95 > 3s).

alexa-sre: creating incident ticket and collecting diagnostic bundle: ```
/scripts/collect-debug.sh --nodes us-east-2a-12,14,19 --since 2026-03-14T23:50Z > /tmp/debug-1802345678.tar.gz
```

jenna-oncall: I'll draft a short customer message and handoff to postmortem owners @kevin-ml, @alexa-sre, and @sara-ops. Handoff note: watch for any slow-drain anomalies; keep routing override for 30m then remove if stable. I'll be offline at 00:15Z (handoff complete). :white_check_mark: 

incident-bot: Incident P1 acknowledged by jenna-oncall, on-call escalations paused.

mike-rt: leaving a follow-up runbook item: add hard enqueue limit + early backpressure when memory high; add canary for scheduler change and better rollback automation.

alexa-sre: I'll schedule postmortem run 03/16 and add timeline + telemetry.

sara-ops: final check: all GPUs reporting healthy, no further OOMs in last 5m, queue drains to baseline. closing immediate mitigation.

tara-cust: noted, thanks team. Please send postmortem and ETA for prevention fix.

mike-rt: acknowledged. postmortem owners will post draft within 48h.

jenna-oncall: closing the handoff. I'll update the incident channel with postmortem link when available. Good work everyone. :tada:
